newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat edges sideways in thin market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat edges sideways in thin market.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat futures slid sideways in a thin market on Thursday in doldrums set by dull seasonal conditions and a dearth of news.
Market leader January 1997 fell 50 cents to A$155.00 a tonne on two trades.

Andrew Szonyi of Perth Commodities and Futures Brokers Pty Ltd said he still saw the marklet picking up. "It should start to happen in the next four weeks ... if we're going to have the traditional seasonal rally through to January," he said.
Szonyi also said a wet harvest in parts of the Australian wheat belt would affect crops, but a reduction by a couple of million tonnes would not affect prices.
The Australian Wheat Board on Thursday cut its indicative cash price for all grades of wheat by A$1.00.
